title: Do Explicit Semantic and Lifecycle Contracts Improve Sanctuary Agent Reliability?
target_platform: Sanctuary mission schema, coordination, lifecycle, preservation and authorization scripts, compared on isolated fixtures with simulated publication (no live remote writes)
proposed_by: Richard (question, after Frank Coyle's talk 'Why Agentic Systems Need Ontologies', https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Sir59K8ZDPU); ChatGPT (comparative research design); registered by claude-code
interest_statement: Determine whether a small, explicit model of entities, relationships and permitted state transitions prevents errors that Sanctuary's current schemas, scripts and operating instructions do not already prevent. This is a research question; it does not assume RDF, OWL, SHACL, Z3, a knowledge graph or a new control plane must be adopted.
hypothesis: Provisional: explicit cross-record and transition checks reduce invalid transitions accepted by the current baseline (A: installed scripts and validators) without materially blocking valid work. A specialized semantic implementation (C: SHACL or a solver) adds value only if it improves coverage, clarity or maintenance over equivalent ordinary-code checks (B), with policy requirements and available evidence held equivalent across B and C. Numeric thresholds and case counts are not yet defined; they are set after the inventory and development phase and frozen before held-out execution.
falsification_criteria: Not yet frozen. To be specified with numeric thresholds after the inventory/development phase and before held-out execution. In outline: the hypothesis fails if B and C accept no fewer held-out invalid transitions than A, or block valid transitions materially more often; C's added value fails if it does not exceed B on coverage, clarity or maintenance at equal rules and evidence. Rules must not be derived from held-out failures. Acceptable outcomes include: existing enforcement sufficient; small script improvements sufficient; semantic validator adds measurable value; evidence insufficient.
baseline_evidence: Sources inspected at abstract/introduction depth only (by ChatGPT): W3C OWL 2 Primer (https://www.w3.org/TR/owl2-primer/); W3C SHACL (https://www.w3.org/TR/shacl/); Solver-Aided Verification of Policy Compliance in Tool-Augmented LLM Agents (https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.20449; authors report fewer policy violations while maintaining task accuracy); VeriMAP, Verification-Aware Planning for Multi-Agent Systems (https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.17109). The talk was inspected through its indexed description and chapters, not a full transcript. Full-text methodological review is part of execution. Candidate historical failures (startup preservation writes, lease reset of a resolved mission to IN_PROGRESS, premature delivery claims, unassessed vs falsified confusion, stale receipt as proof of persistence) are not yet confirmed from repository records. Synthesis: LEARNING/research/semantic_lifecycle_contracts/README.md.
experiment: 1) Inventory existing enforcement: map each relevant invariant to the code that enforces it; examine Agentic OS capabilities; separate missing from bypassable checks. 2) Define a small domain model (candidates: Mission, Attempt, Evidence, Verdict, Authorization, Lease, SourceRevision, Export, RemoteReceipt), only the relationships the selected cases need, marking trusted observations vs agent assertions. 3) Compare A (current scripts), B (minimal ordinary-code preconditions/transition checks) and C (one semantic implementation, SHACL or solver, only if research shows a fit) on identical cases. 4) Use confirmed historical failures plus valid and already-fixed counterparts as development examples. 5) Freeze a bounded evaluation (invalid/valid transitions, stale/missing evidence, interruption/resume, duplicate requests, concurrent change between validation and execution; rejection before side effect) and run held-out cases on isolated fixtures with simulated publication.
phases: Freeze thresholds, case counts and budget
Held-out comparison of A, B and C
score_basis: Provisional planning estimates, not measured ROI. Leverage 4: potentially reusable reliability improvement. Depth 4: comparative test of where enforcement belongs. Cost weight 1 and friction 3: moderate experimental and integration complexity (inventory, fixtures, possible new dependency). Priority = (4x4)/(1x3) = 5.33. Zero model calls in a CPU evaluator must not be read as the total mission cost.
strategic_intent: Decide on evidence whether Sanctuary needs explicit semantic or lifecycle contracts, small script improvements, or nothing new.
design_constraints: Do not assume adoption of RDF, OWL, SHACL, Z3, a knowledge graph or a new control plane
Select one semantic implementation, not every stack
Hold policy requirements and evidence equivalent across B and C
Isolated fixtures and simulated publication only; no live destructive operations or remote writes
Freeze thresholds before held-out execution; never derive rules from held-out failures
A deterministic fixture study cannot establish improved real-agent behaviour
An ontology does not provide locking, authorization or idempotency by describing them

readiness.assessment: Registration ready. Execution requires an inventory, a bounded design, verified dependencies and an explicit resource budget.
missing_prerequisites: Verified SHACL or solver dependency (only if C is selected)

model_routing.frontier_escalation_condition: Domain-model design or held-out assessment disagreement
model_routing.routing_guidance: Inventory and fixture work are deterministic; model use is for design and review. Any live-agent token test needs separate justification and a bounded budget.
